title: Lagrange fast-path re-enablement — drop SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD via div_rem_auto
description:
With the preceding `div_rem_auto` primitive landed (issue `ae0c7e1f`), `batch_evaluate_subproduct` and `interpolate_fast` can finally realise their `O(n log² n)` asymptote. This close-out task drops `SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD` below `usize::MAX`, re-benches the Lagrange paths, and refreshes the module-docstring tables.

## Background

The `interpolate_fast` + `batch_evaluate_subproduct` machinery already ships (closed in session 3 via `2e7db385` + work-in-tree from `3cff65f7`). The blocker was `FieldPoly::div_rem` being schoolbook `O((n−m)·m)`; the subproduct-tree reduction phase invokes it repeatedly. With `ae0c7e1f` adding `div_rem_fast` + `div_rem_auto`, the tree reduction is now `O(M(n) log n)` in aggregate. Tuning `SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD` below `usize::MAX` activates the public `FieldPoly::batch_evaluate` dispatcher's fast lane.

## Scope

### 1. Route the subproduct tree through `div_rem_auto`

In `batch_evaluate_subproduct` (`crates/gf2-core/src/field/poly.rs` around line 990–1050), replace `FieldPoly::div_rem` calls with `FieldPoly::div_rem_auto` so the reduction phase uses the fast path above the tuned threshold. Where the tree helper generic-dispatches over arbitrary `F: FiniteField` (not `TwoAdicField`), keep the schoolbook fallback; specialise with `F: TwoAdicField` where that's required.

### 2. Tune `SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD`

Lower from `usize::MAX` at `poly.rs:1776` to the empirical crossover point discovered by rerunning the `field_poly_batch_evaluate_fp65537` bench group after step 1. Plausible target: 32–128.

### 3. Tune `INTERPOLATE_THRESHOLD`

Currently `16` at `poly_interpolate.rs:92` (kept as a conservative pre-enablement margin). Re-check against the refreshed benchmark; adjust if the new crossover has shifted.

### 4. Regenerate benchmark snapshot tables

Update the "Benchmark snapshot" section in the `poly.rs` module docstring with fresh numbers for:
- `batch_evaluate` (now measures the dispatcher's actual fast-path behaviour above the threshold)
- `interpolate_fast` vs `interpolate`
Keep the existing `subproduct` and `naive` columns for baseline continuity.

### 5. Refresh `dev/plans/field_poly_module_overview.md`

Remove the "Known gaps and future work — `SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD = usize::MAX`" paragraph that said the fast path was unrealised. Replace with a short note that records the tuned threshold and the landing commits (`ae0c7e1f` for fast div, this task for threshold tuning).

### 6. Proptest coverage

Add (or uplift) a proptest that runs `batch_evaluate` across input sizes that straddle the new `SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD` and asserts agreement with a naive Horner sweep on ≥ 500 random inputs over `Fp<65537>`. Covers the dispatcher both below and above the new threshold.

## Success criteria

- `cargo fmt --all` clean
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --release -- -D warnings` clean
- `cargo test --workspace --all-features --release` passes, release test execution ≤ 60 s
- `batch_evaluate` achieves measured sub-quadratic slope at `n, k ≥ 2·SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD` on `Fp<65537>` (bench table in docs is the evidence)
- `SUBPRODUCT_THRESHOLD` and `INTERPOLATE_THRESHOLD` values tuned from data and documented in the module docstring + overview doc
- No residual "fast path unrealised" language in docs

## Dependencies

- `ae0c7e1f` (fast FieldPoly div_rem + `div_rem_auto` dispatcher)
- `e0b6f940` (NTT mul) — done
- `224a7d9e` (module docstring + bench scaffold) — done
